business_problem: KION needed a safer and more efficient way to automate warehouse operations at scale while reducing process delays, deployment risk, and the trial-and-error required to introduce autonomous robots into complex facilities.
solution_summary: Accenture and KION built an AI-robotics design and simulation workflow that trains warehouse robots before they are deployed into live environments. Working through the Accenture NVIDIA Business Group, the team combines NVIDIA Mega, an Omniverse Blueprint, with KION's supply-chain expertise to create digital twins of entire warehouse systems, including conveyors, pallets, forklifts, autonomous mobile robots, humanoids, robotic arms, and human workers. These digital environments simulate physical interactions, Black Friday demand spikes, and layout changes so robot behaviors can be tuned before go-live. The platform predicts and adapts to real-world operating conditions, helping KION reduce errors, protect worker safety, and optimize throughput. Instead of testing automation only on the warehouse floor, KION can iterate in simulation first and then move more reliable AI-driven robots into production supply-chain operations.

data_flow: Warehouse layouts, assets, and operational scenarios are modeled as digital twins inside the Omniverse environment. NVIDIA Mega runs simulations that test robot behaviors against those conditions, and the resulting adjustments are pushed into autonomous robots before live deployment in warehouse operations.
integration_points: warehouse demand scenarios such as Black Friday sales
business_outcome: KION can validate and tune robotic workflows before rollout, helping warehouses lower operating friction, improve safety, and increase fulfillment efficiency while preparing workers for higher-value oversight roles.
